### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **103** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/sharing_rule.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5da2e88818a006145330e3f323759ebef4d6ca87`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/sharing_rule.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 34 pages)`
- **21** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **149** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5da2e88818a006145330e3f323759ebef4d6ca87` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6351373e631ef16f8f2e1b7c7670d9b972f89524` — the merge of head `e0baaa76c69c4d53e43cad8002f7cda487ccd0b3` into base `5da2e88818a006145330e3f323759ebef4d6ca87`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6351373e631ef16f8f2e1b7c7670d9b972f89524 && git checkout 6351373e631ef16f8f2e1b7c7670d9b972f89524
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 5da2e88818a006145330e3f323759ebef4d6ca87 e0baaa76c69c4d53e43cad8002f7cda487ccd0b3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 5da2e88818a006145330e3f323759ebef4d6ca87 && git merge --no-ff e0baaa76c69c4d53e43cad8002f7cda487ccd0b3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 5da2e88818a006145330e3f323759ebef4d6ca87
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 5da2e88818a006145330e3f323759ebef4d6ca87` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e3658abc263d3e29a4cf3f36fe10327fa181f80f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/declared-sharing-rules.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-apply.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts, .changeset/23952-declared-sharing-rules-registry.md + packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/field-recipient.test.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-apply.declared-rule-mirrors.test.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-apply.test.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.declared-rule-mirrors.integration.test.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.remote-face.integration.test.ts, packages/lint/src/{authoring-rules,rule-explanations,validate-sharing-rule-enforceability}.ts and their two tests, packages/qa/dogfood/test/{authz-conformance.matrix,expression-conformance.ledger,org-scoped-sharing-rule-listing.dogfood.test,showcase-d3-d4-capabilities.dogfood.test,showcase-declarative-rbac-seeding.dogfood.test}.ts, packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack-seeder-declaration-copy.test.ts, packages/spec/liveness/sharing_rule.json, packages/spec/scripts/liveness/proof-registry.mts (the whole 27-file diff: on the narrowing face no path is a remainder); cited code read: packages/rest/src/sharing-routes.ts (the DELETE door and its `handleError`), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/objects/sys-sharing-rule.object.ts (`managed_by` readonly), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/objects/sys-record-share.object.ts (indexes), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts (the grant upsert key), packages/platform-objects/src/system/migration-flag.ts (`recordDataMigrationRun`), packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.standard-error-code-batch-members-retired.ts (the semantic-entry precedent), the deleted packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/bootstrap-declared-sharing-rules.ts at the merge base, docs/adr/0131 (D2, D6, D10, D13, D14), docs/adr/0112 (D1–D5 and the 2026-08-17 flat-door amendment), docs/adr/0087 (the disposition vocabulary), docs/adr/0057 D6, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-doc-authoring.mjs, scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs and scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/{contract-review,execution-duties,filing-gate}.md.

Rendered by an isolated at-tier reviewer subagent of the adopting seat (`epic:#15194`), read-only, from the card (#23952 body and all four comments), the rulings it cites (β 6216760903 and the stage-0 addendum 6100442578 on #15204, the hand-off 6220693269, decision #24352 ruled C in 6251599171), the PR body, its file list, the net diff `origin/main...e3658abc2` fetched into a reviewer-owned ref, and the head's check-runs. Not read: the dispatch order or the dispatching seat's conclusions.

**Check-runs on the head, as read (the 2026-10-18 17:14Z run, last re-read 17:43Z):** 40 check-runs — 32 `success`, among them the required contexts `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, every `Type Check ·` lane including `Type Check · workspace`, `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Check PR Size`, the three card/branch claim guards, and `Test Core` 1/6, 2/6, 5/6, 6/6; 6 `skipped` by design (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, the dogfood matrix shard rows, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Packed-tarball smoke); `Test Core` 3/6 and 4/6 still `in_progress` at the last read; 0 `failure`. The adopting seat re-reads the two open `Test Core` shards before any landing act; this record's verdict does not depend on them (it fails on the items below).

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, named right or wrong.

**(a) `DELETE /api/v1/sharing/rules/:idOrName` on a declared rule: 204 → 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`.** RIGHT as an answer: a declared rule has no row (`sharing-rule-service.ts:967-981`: `findRuleRow` first, then the declared projection, then the throw); a silent 204 would read as success while the rule keeps granting, and a 404 would contradict the same caller's `GET`/list one call earlier — the #7795 reasoning, carried over exactly. Refusing a system context alike is right: there is nothing to delete and code is changed in code. The throw is the service family's prefix convention (`Error('PERMISSION_DENIED: …')`), which the door maps at `packages/rest/src/sharing-routes.ts:578-580` to `res.status(403).json({ code: 'PERMISSION_DENIED', error })` — the family's flat dialect, a live envelope under ADR-0112 (the 2026-08-17 #9232 amendment: `code` is the closed `StandardErrorCode` member the status derives; the body POSITION is owned by the `check:route-envelope` ratchet, not by this PR). So at the REST door the answer is `403` with `code: PERMISSION_DENIED` — the right code and the right status, and no new door shape. Also right: `getRule`/`listRules`/`evaluateRule` by NAME keep working for the same caller (pinned at `sharing-rule.test.ts:2218-2220` and in the dogfood listing test), so the 403 is not a lie. WRONG — the pins: `sharing-rule.test.ts:2221` and `:2223` pin the refusal with `rejects.toThrow(/^PERMISSION_DENIED: …/)` and `/^PERMISSION_DENIED/`, a message regex. This file's own #7795 block (`:1320-1360`) states the rule that governs here — "a loose `.toThrow()` — or even `/PERMISSION_DENIED/` as a substring — cannot tell them apart" — and pins with `refusalCodeOf` (the exact ADR-0112 token), `expect(HttpStatusErrorCodeMap[403]).toBe(code)` (the status SOURCED, not restated), `not.toBe(HttpStatusErrorCodeMap[404])` / `'RULE_NOT_FOUND'`, and "the refusal leaves … every tenant's grants intact". None of the four is asserted for the declared-rule refusal: no pin sources the status, none asserts the token exactly, none asserts the declaration's grants are left standing (the throw precedes `purgeGrants`, so they are — unpinned). Under this repo's review rules a message regex alone is not a pin. → blocking item 1.

**(b) Grants of a declared rule carry `source_id` = the rule's NAME; the ceremony renames before it deletes.** RIGHT. `projectDeclaredRule` gives the projection `id: rule.name` (`sharing-rule-service.ts:150-166`) and every grant read and write goes through `ruleGrantScope(rule)` (reconcile, reconcileForRecord, `purgeGrants`, the retired-recipient revoke), so the service has one code path for id-keyed and name-keyed grants (β item 5 (c)). An organization-authored rule keeps its minted `srule_…` id as `source_id` (pinned `sharing-rule.test.ts` "an organization-authored rule keeps working through its row"). The ceremony's `runDeclaredRuleMirrorDeletion` (`organization-ownership-apply.ts:2561-2651`) works in the ruled order and the order is provable from the code, not only the prose: (1) mirrors read by the departure's own selector (`:2503-2518`, `managed_by` package/platform and `customized` not true, NULL and organization-stamped rows alike), (2) the block on a mirror whose rule no installed package declares while grants still name it, nothing written (`:2586-2596`), (3) the rename of every `sys_record_share` row with `source = 'rule'` and `source_id` = the mirror's id to the mirror's NAME (`:2598-2613`), (4) the verification that zero grants still name any mirror id, which THROWS before any delete (`:2614-2622`), (5) the delete by id with the selector re-asserted and a count to zero (`:2626-2643`). Pinned: the write-log order `lastRename` before `firstDelete` (`organization-ownership-apply.declared-rule-mirrors.test.ts:253`); every grant resolves by name or by a kept row's id, the customized copy and the organization's rule untouched (unit `:181-255`, integration `:255-262`, `organization-ownership-apply.test.ts:892-924`); idempotent — a second run finds no mirror and writes nothing to either table (`:257`); the checkpointed re-run on a database certified by a seeding release (`:266`, the hotcrm `dev.db` case); the undeclared-with-grants block writes nothing (`:288`); the grant-less undeclared mirror goes like every fate-2 mirror; the no-registry block; the walled organization-stamped copy goes and the customized one stays (`:321`). A blocked re-run cannot leave a stale certification: every ledger write goes through `recordDataMigrationRun`, which sets `verified_at` only when `passed` (`migration-flag.ts:198`), so the first checkpoint write of a re-run un-verifies the marker and a blocked run leaves it un-verified — since #24325 that database is not served, which is the ruled posture. The rename cannot collide: `sys_record_share` carries no unique index on `(source, source_id)` (`sys-record-share.object.ts:268-277`) and `SharingService.grant` upserts on `(object, record, recipient, source)` (`sharing-service.ts:1417`), and while a mirror stands it answers for its name (the `held` set), so no name-keyed grant exists before the deletion; afterwards the first reconcile adopts the renamed rows by `(record_id, recipient_id)`. Partial failure between (3) and (5) is safe: the next run counts zero grants on those mirrors and deletes them. One gap, NOT blocking, recorded for the dev: `DeclaredSharingRulesPort.names()` (`organization-ownership.ts:802-818`) answers the REGISTRY's item names, not the rules enforcement SERVES — a declared rule whose translation is skipped (unlowerable condition, unmappable recipient) resolves as declared, its mirror's grants are renamed to a name no projection serves, and the next boot's sweep revokes them. The 17.x seeder never seeded such a rule, so the case needs a condition the 17.x compiler lowered and the v18 compiler refuses; narrow, but the ceremony's own principle ("deleting it would withdraw that access on the operator's behalf") says the port should answer served names, or the step should warn when it renames onto an unserved one.

**(c) The walled posture.** No cross-tenant read or write of GRANTS: `ruleGrantScope` stamps `organization_id` on every read and write of a walled projection's grants, `criteriaContext(rule)` (`:1432-1436`) threads the projection's organization into the record query, `declaredScopesFor` (`:882-887`) gives an organization-scoped caller only its own projection and a system or platform caller every known one (by authority), `evaluateRule` on a declared name under a wall runs one pass per projection and reports one rule; pinned ("one organization's reconcile leaves the other organization's grants of the same rule standing", "the sweep keeps each organization's served grants"). The holders read (`:862-871`) is a SYSTEM_CTX read of `name` and `organization_id` across organizations, used only to compute shadowing — no row content crosses a tenant, and nothing a tenant did not already see through `adminOrgScope`. An organization created after boot is served from its creation (`addDeclaredRuleScope`, the creation middleware; pinned). WRONG — the scope set is allowed to be INCOMPLETE and the service cannot tell "unknown" from "none": `resolveDeclaredRuleScopes` (`sharing-plugin.ts:88-110`) returns `[]` when `sys_organization` cannot be read (`:105`) and otherwise enumerates at most `DECLARED_RULE_ORGANIZATION_SCAN_LIMIT = 500` organizations (`:77`, `:98`) with no `orderBy`. At `kernel:bootstrapped` the plugin then runs `sweepOrphanedRuleGrants()` (`sharing-plugin.ts:1108`), whose `liveDeclared` set is built from `declaredRules(SYSTEM_CTX, {})` (`sharing-rule-service.ts:1095-1098`): for every organization NOT in `declaredScopes`, every grant whose `source_id` is a declared rule's name is revoked (`:1113`). Two consequences, both new: (i) a transient `sys_organization` read failure at boot revokes every declared rule's grants in every organization of a walled deployment — the very rows the ceremony just renamed under item 5 (c) — until a later boot's backfill re-materialises them; (ii) the 501st and later organizations are never served (no enforcement there) and have their grants revoked at every boot. Under the seeder the same failure left the already-seeded rows standing and their id-keyed grants live, and the bound only delayed seeding; the plugin's own comment ("an organization past the bound is covered by the organization-creation hook and by the next boot", `:74-76`) is false in the read model, and the changeset's "no declared rule is served until the next boot" does not say the boot sweep withdraws their grants. A read failure must not be a revocation. → blocking item 2.

**(d) A stored row of the declared name answers for it.** INHERITED, not new: the seeder's `defineRule` upsert looked the row up by `{ name }` under SYSTEM_CTX (any organization's row) under `single`, and by `{ name, organization_id }` per organization under a wall, and never overwrote a `managed_by: admin` or `customized` row (`sharing-rule-service.ts:672-718`, the #2909 seed-not-clobber), so a same-name stored row has answered for a declared name since #2909; the `held` key (`:869`: name alone under `single`, `name::organization` under a wall) reproduces that key exactly. SAFE against forgery: `isDeclaredSharingRule` needs `managed_by === 'package'` AND `id === name`; `managed_by` is `readonly` (the engine strips it from non-system payloads, `sys-sharing-rule.object.ts:248-253`) and row ids are minted. Two consequences ARE new, both acknowledged in the PR body, neither blocking, both owed to the item (b) decision card (③ item 1): an administrator can now CREATE a same-name row where no seeded row exists (before, the row existed and the edit stamped `customized`), which switches the declaration off in that scope — silent shadowing by NAME, the trap the dev names; and the shadowed declaration's name-keyed grants stand until the next boot's sweep, because `bindRuleRebindTriggers` reconciles only the written row's id (`sharing-plugin.ts:456-466`) — a one-restart over-sharing window the seeder era did not have (deactivating the seeded row purged its grants at once through `evaluateRule`).

**(e) `DECLARED_SHARING_RULE_SEEDER_RUNS = false` and decision #24352 → C.** RIGHT and consistent. The constant flips in this change and no other (`organization-ownership-inventory.ts:676`; the hand-off 6220693269's one order), `advisoryDepartureReason` therefore answers `null` for the mirrors and they hold certification until the step deletes them (β items 1–2: the marker keeps meaning zero NULL rows); the integration test asserts the constant against what a served boot actually writes (`:222`) and that eleven mirrors with grants are renamed and deleted to `[complete, blocking, advisory] = [true, 0, unattributable]` (`:243`). Decision #24352 → C (6251599171) makes UNATTRIBUTABLE rows block in stage 8c-0, which the ruling orders after this PR's ceremony half and before 8c-1; this PR keeps them advisory (`advisory = after.summary.unattributableRows`, asserted as `unattributable` in the integration test) — consistent with the ruled sequencing, and the 8c-0 PR will flip that one pin. β item 2 is thus met in the two ruled steps.

**Other surfaces the diff moves, all RIGHT:** `GET /api/v1/sharing/rules` lists a declared projection with `id` = name, `managed_by: 'package'`, `customized: false`, `organization_id` null under `single` / the organization under a wall (the seeded row listed with the same fields and a minted id before); `POST …/:name/evaluate` works by name (pinned in the dogfood listing test); the boot writes zero `sys_sharing_rule` rows in every posture and a declared rule still enforces, with the positive control that removing the declaration stops the grant (`sharing-rule.test.ts` "POSITIVE CONTROL"; the card's first pin); the per-record hooks, the business-unit recompute, the backfill and the sweep all list through `listRules` (A1 of the PR body holds on read); `@objectstack/lint`'s verdicts change prose only, rule ids and severities unchanged (`patch`); the `sharing_rule` liveness producer anchors are re-pointed to `declared-sharing-rules.ts#translateDeclaredSharingRule` (evidence pointers, `Spec property liveness` green); `DefineSharingRuleInput.managedBy` keeps its meaning with no in-repo producer (the acceptance note is right). WRONG — a claim in the cited code: `declared-sharing-rules.ts:7-9` says the seeder's "retirement note is the ADR-0087 `sharing-rule-declared-mirror-retired` entry"; no such entry exists anywhere in the tree at this head (the only occurrence is that citation), the changeset's marker says "No ADR-0087 id covers this and this diff adds none", and card item 2 asked for the retirement note to be written as the ADR-0087 entry ("the seeder is machinery, not an authorable shape, so the ADR-0087 entry is the note"). A code comment citing a registry entry that does not exist is a decision nobody can find. → blocking item 3 (with ②).

### ② Semver level

The changeset bumps `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` `minor`, `@objectstack/cli` `minor`, `@objectstack/lint` `patch`, declares breaking through the `!` summary and the `**BREAKING**` banner, and carries the `adr-0087:` disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The LEVELS match what the diff publishes: both runtime packages break (the DELETE refusal; `sys_sharing_rule` no longer holding a row per declared rule; the ceremony deleting the copies), shipped as `minor` under the launch-window convention `check-changeset-no-major` enforces; lint is prose-only. `Check Changeset` is `success` on the head.

The `Clause-②:` line is WRONG and MUST read `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, at the start of a line of its own, on BOTH carriers — the PR body and `.changeset/23952-declared-sharing-rules-registry.md:9`. `DELETE /api/v1/sharing/rules/:idOrName` on a declared rule narrows a published REST accept set (204, the seeded row deleted → 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`): `filing-gate.md` — "REST/数据门收窄亦算"; `execution-duties.md` — a card narrowing a published accept set is `Clause-②: no` and owes a contract-review-tier review before the queue; `contract-review.md` and `record-recognisers.mjs` — the narrowing face is keyed on the one spelling `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` written at the start of a line in the PR body and the changeset. Two things follow from the bare `no` as committed: `reviewFace` on this file list defers to the changeset's line and reads the DECLARATION face (`TIER_DEFAULT`), so this at-tier record does not stand on the committed tree until the line is corrected ("exact, never a floor"); and `check-adr-0087-registration` reads this PR's breaking-ness only off the `!` and banner prose the author happened to type — the carrier that does not depend on prose is the arm. The narrowing is written FROM → TO in the changeset: `DELETE /api/v1/sharing/rules/:idOrName` for a declared rule — FROM `204` with the seeded row deleted and re-seeded at the next boot, TO `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`; `sys_sharing_rule` — FROM one `managed_by: package` row per declared rule, TO none (the ceremony deletes the copies; Setup's object list no longer shows them).

The ADR-0087 disposition marker is held by a detector miss and must be re-decided with the arm: the body already names the operator's re-run (`:25`, "Re-run `--apply` with a fresh plan") and the FROM → TO above, written in the house label convention, is exactly what the gate's branch 1 reads as a prescription — ADR-0087: "`no-migration-prescription` is refused by a body that carries a migration prescription". The honest disposition is `registered sharing-rule-declared-mirror-retired`: a `SemanticMigration` at `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.sharing-rule-declared-mirror-retired.ts`, in the shape of `18.standard-error-code-batch-members-retired.ts` (a wire-level narrowing with no stored-metadata rewrite — "this entry is the notification channel"), its `surface` the DELETE refusal, the deleted copies and the Setup list, its `replacement` "change or remove the rule in its declaration; an organization's own rule is deleted as before", its `reason` ADR-0131 D2 / C3 stage 9 and ruling β. That one file makes the docblock citation true, discharges card item 2's retirement note and D13's "each retirement … is an ADR-0087 entry", and the gate re-verifies `registered` (the id resolves and is new in the diff — it would be). It is a `packages/spec/src` touch outside the claim's file surface: the claim's ⛔ targeted registering `sharing_rule` as a metadata kind, which the dev's A2 showed unnecessary; the adopting seat widens the claim for this one file or routes it to the spec seat — either way the entry is the card's item 2. If the seat instead rules the entry not owed, the citation at `declared-sharing-rules.ts:9` is deleted and `no-migration-prescription` stays, with the FROM → TO stated outside the label convention; the comment and the changeset must agree, and today they contradict each other.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry in the os-dev-report (6252786437), answered or escalated.

1. **Item (b) — what switching off a vendor's declared sharing rule means** (`open_questions[0]`, the addendum's (b), β item 5 (b)): not settled by governing text — ADR-0131 D6 charts regimes O, C and E and names none for `sharing_rule`; ADR-0057 D6 speaks only to seeding. The dev built no disable mechanism and recommends A (regime C: the tenant-less activation ledger, name-shadowing retired after the mirrors go). Answer: right to build nothing in this PR (the card: "it does not block items 2–5"). ESCALATED to the adopting seat, which files the decision card the card body owes ("the epic PM files a decision card"); the card must carry the two consequences measured in ①(d) — a freshly created same-name row now switches a vendor rule off silently, and the shadowed declaration's grants stand until the next restart — as evidence, not only the inherited shadow.
